findings.claim: Retrying the same payment request creates a second charge instead of returning the original charge outcome, allowing clients or infrastructure retries to duplicate a financial side effect.
evidence: evals/cases/case_02/src/payments.py:14-18 unconditionally inserts and commits a new charges row on every process_payment call; it never checks for an existing request_id.
evals/cases/case_02/src/db.py:9-13 defines request_id as NOT NULL but does not enforce uniqueness, so the database permits multiple charges for the same logical request.
Running pytest -q evals/cases/case_02 produced one failure and one pass: two calls with request_id req-123 caused test_idempotency.py:18 to observe count == 2 rather than the required count == 1.
